reviewed_by: Claude general-purpose subagent, blind judgment reviewer, post-fix stale re-review batch 2, 2026-08-02

samples_reviewed.question_text: Look at the 5×6 array. How many squares are shaded in all?
Shade all the squares inside the 2×6 rectangle. How many squares did you shade in all?

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The competency is 'illustrate division through equal distribution of objects,' but no sample shows objects being distributed; seed 42's 'What is 70 ÷ 10?' is a bare numeral fact and seed 50 is actually a multiplication array question.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Equal-distribution illustration never renders across all 9 samples; the closest visual content, seed 50's 'Look at the 5×6 array' and seed 55's 'Shade all the squares inside the 2×6 rectangle,' are multiplication array tasks, not division.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Seed 50 and seed 55 require array-shading/counting reasoning (5×6, 2×6) that is cognitively a different skill from the bare division-fact recall in seed 42's '70 ÷ 10', so the batch's reasoning demand is inconsistent.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Variation is limited to bare 'X ÷ Y' equations (seeds 42-46, 51, 85) plus two off-topic multiplication-array items (50, 55); no word-problem or picture variant showing a set of objects split into groups ever appears.

competency_alignment.rationale: Seed 50 ('Look at the 5×6 array. How many squares are shaded in all?') and seed 55 ('Shade all the squares inside the 2×6 rectangle') build multiplication-array counting, a distinct operation from division-by-equal-distribution.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Division facts stay in a reasonable grade-2 range (seed 42's 70÷10=7 up to seed 45's 30÷3=10), but 2 of 9 samples test unrelated multiplication magnitudes (30, 12) instead of any division scale at all.
